analysis.investment_thesis: Anlon Healthcare shows attractive headline ratios (ROE 25.5%, OM 33.7%) but operating cash flow has been negative for 4 consecutive years while reported profits grew — a classic mismatch that signals working capital bloat or earnings quality concerns. At a 616 Cr micro-cap with volatile revenue (57→113→67→120 Cr), short listed history, and deeply negative FCF (-23 Cr in FY25), this fails my basic test of a predictable compounder.
key_strengths: Strong reported margins (OM 33.7%, ROCE 38.1%) and ROE 25.5%
D/E down to 0.27 post recent equity infusion (equity 21→80 Cr)
Niche API/intermediates portfolio across multiple therapeutic areas
key_risks: OCF negative in 4/4 years despite rising PAT — earnings quality suspect
Revenue highly volatile (FY24 dropped to 67 Cr from 113 Cr) — not a steady compounder
Micro-cap, recently listed, unproven promoter track record; promoter holding only 52.7%
red_flags: Profit of 21 Cr but operating cash flow of -23 Cr in FY25 — ~44 Cr gap
Zero free cash generation across entire visible history
Debt still 67 Cr, 83% of equity book, in a capex-hungry API business
Promoter stake just above 50% — below my >55% threshold
analysis.detailed_analysis: The business superficially screens well — 33.7% operating margin, 38% ROCE, P/E of 17.75 — but when I look past the ratios I cannot reconcile the profit statement with the cash flow statement. PAT cumulatively over FY23-25 is ~37 Cr, yet cumulative OCF is roughly -29 Cr. That means every rupee of reported profit has been locked up in receivables or inventory, a pattern I've seen too often in small API/chemical companies and one I refuse to underwrite. Revenue swinging from 113 Cr (FY23) to 67 Cr (FY24) back to 120 Cr (FY25) also tells me this is a lumpy order-driven business, not the predictable consumer-facing demand I prefer.\n\nThe balance sheet cleanup (equity jumping 21→80 Cr in FY25) is almost entirely IPO proceeds, not retained earnings, and debt at 67 Cr is still meaningful for a 120 Cr revenue company. Promoter holding at 52.7% is at the lower end of acceptable and will likely dilute further given the negative FCF trajectory. This is outside my circle of competence — API manufacturing for 13 therapeutic areas is not a moat I can verify — and the fundamentals do not yet earn the benefit of the doubt. I pass.
